items.title: PM warns Australians not to expect 'big changes' to capital gains tax
items.description: Small business owners are urging Labor to rethink more than just the eligibility thresholds for capital gains tax concessions.

items.title: Iran and US trade air strikes after Trump dismisses Hormuz deal
items.description: The US president has repeatedly said the end of the war is close, but told media at a cabinet meeting on Wednesday he was not yet satisfied by the negotiations and the US is not discussing easing sanctions, one of Tehran's key demands.

items.title: Details of first NZYQ Nauru deal payment revealed
items.description: Details of the secretive NZYQ resettlement deal have emerged, including a breakdown of the government's first payment.

items.title: How tax rules benefit top earners by $700,000 but median earners by $5,700
items.description: Commonwealth Treasury secretary Jenny Wilkinson says the average top income earner benefited from the existing investment tax arrangements to the tune of $700,000 over their lifetime, versus just $5,700 for median income earners.

items.title: The 14 risk factors for dementia Jane wishes she knew earlier
items.description: Too many Australians still see dementia as an inevitability, according to new data but there is a list of steps you can take to reduce the risks.

items.title: 'I'm about to explode': UK hits 35C in spring as warning issued
items.description: As the mercury climbed around the United Kingdom this week and new May maximums were recorded in multiple areas, the once-welcome sunshine is sparking alarm among many people.

items.title: Austrian man gets 15 years' jail for Taylor Swift concert terror plot
items.description: The concert plot was thwarted, but Austrian authorities still cancelled Swift’s three performances in August 2024.

items.title: Trump says Murdoch indicated he would 'handle' newspaper's Epstein story
items.description: In refiling his lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal, the US president alleges Rupert Murdoch indicated a story about his ties with Jeffrey Epstein would not be published.

items.title: Labor campaigned on 'integrity' so the NACC should be enjoying public trust by now
items.description: In an extraordinary irony, the National Anti-Corruption Commission has become best known for "own goals", rocked by internal scandals and attracting a litany of complaints.

items.title: AFP defends public arrest of Ben Roberts-Smith
items.description: The Australian Federal Police has detailed intelligence surrounding Ben Roberts-Smith's arrest, pushing back against criticisms of its public nature.

items.title: Australian to join 'scary as hell' mission to rescue Laos villagers from cave
items.description: A diver describes the "emotional moment" when he found a group of men alive after they were trapped for more than a week in a Laos cave, while a South Australian renowned for his ability to navigate tight spaces joins the rescue mission.

items.title: Insect repellent may not always keep mozzies away, study suggests
items.description: Scientists have found that mosquitoes in the lab can be trained to connect the smell of a widely used repellent with food, but repellents are still the best way to protect yourself.

items.title: Government sues 3M Australia for $2 billion over PFAS contamination
items.description: The Commonwealth is launching its largest-ever legal claim, suing the manufacturer of a firefighting foam containing PFAS chemicals that contaminated 28 Defence Force bases across Australia.

items.title: Friday news quiz: A drone drama, a 'dream job' and an old insult making a comeback
items.description: Your hopes of passing might come crashing down like so many drones in a harbour. But it's still worth a try.

items.title: The Aussie rocker who mastered the video game needle drop
items.description: Melbourne's Johnny Galvatron gave up the rockstar life to become a BAFTA-winning game developer. Now, his studio's latest release, Mixtape, re-imagines the music game as an eclectic playlist of genres and mechanics.

items.title: Growing garlic is one of life's slower lessons
items.description: In April 2020, I put my first cloves into the ground. Here's what I learnt over the next five years of trying — and often failing — to grow good garlic.

items.title: What does it mean to be the best jack of all trades, but master of none?
items.description: Elite athletes are constantly striving for perfection — an extra millisecond shaved off their time or another centimetre on their distance — but for heptathletes like Tori West, the equation is a little bit harder.

items.title: Aussies facing 'most important day' of World Championship campaign
items.description: The threat of relegation hangs over the Australian men's rugby sevens squad ahead of the final two rounds of the World Championship series.

items.title: 'Unfair' Women's Origin timing criticised as Blues sweep Maroons aside
items.description: The captains of New South Wales and Queensland question the timing of the Women's State of Origin series after the Blues completed an historic clean sweep.

items.title: Private landowners fill the void as return of Aboriginal land stalls
items.description: It has been two decades since substantial land hand-backs in Tasmania, so private owners are doing it instead. Near Hobart, a piece of land that was once a dumping ground is being restored.

items.title: Need for mine's hybrid power plant 'embarrassing', outback MP says
items.description: An international energy company is building Australia's largest off-grid renewable hybrid power facility, as a state politician criticises the need for it.

items.title: Meet the Iranians who gather every night outside Khamenei's house
items.description: Outside the Tehran compound that was home to now-dead Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei, hundreds of his supporters gather every night to mourn the only leader many of them have ever known.

items.title: Tasmanian MLC may escalate complaint over 'appalling' leaked email
items.description: Ruth Forrest says she is "deeply disappointed" about a lack of government response over a leaked email and is considering referring a complaint to WorkSafe Tasmania and parliament's Privileges Committee.

items.title: Work about to begin on $3.6b Olympic Stadium as protesters vow to stay put
items.description: The Queensland government wants site work to begin on Brisbane's $3.6 billion Olympic stadium on Monday as residents plan a court challenge and Indigenous protesters refuse to move.

items.title: At least 16 students dead as fire tears through Kenyan girls school
items.description: The blaze reportedly started when a student set a mattress on fire inside the school's dormitory, with a further 79 students taken to hospital with injuries.
